doc.title: Mickey Roker interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Advice to young drummers: cherish friends and stay clean
summary: Roker urges staying away from drugs and cigarettes and cherishing friends who will call you for work.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Well I want to ask you as we kind of close here, if you had an encouragement that you could give to young drummers on the way up. I know you talked about hearing the music live.

Well I think that the first thing they should do is cherish their friends. Because without their friends, you have nothing. I think you should stay clean, don’t use no drugs, don’t use no drugs, don’t smoke no cigarettes, you know, and then your mind is free to learn music. See ‘cause you have to have a free mind. You can’t be bogged down with sidetracks. You know what I’m saying? But the main thing is to cherish your friends man, because they’re the only people that’s going to call you for work is your friends. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
